items.title: Meta Pinky Promises Its Smart Glasses Will Be Private Soon
items.summary: The company is bringing its Private Processing encryption service to its much-maligned smart glasses.
items.content:
Meta knows you probably have some privacy concerns about its smart glasses .

At its annual Meta Connect event today in Menlo Park, California, the company announced plans to incorporate its siloed AI processing scheme known as Private Processing into its Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses. The feature, designed for WhatsApp last year, allows the glasses’ AI assistant to get to know you and fulfill your requests without Meta accessing any of your data.

“Most of the time, glasses are helping you see well, protecting your eyes and complementing your look, and that’s it,” Meta wrote in its press release, perhaps somewhat underselling the monumental historic significance of vision-correcting lenses as a technology. “But AI glasses have the capacity to provide superpowers like translating a conversation or summarizing notes or a conversation.” So the company says it sought to answer the question: “How do you build a hyper-personalized AI that knows your world deeply with enhanced privacy?”

Private Processing is designed to enable AI cloud processing that protects data from all outside parties, including Meta itself. For its smart glasses, Private Processing could theoretically enable "private" chat interactions with Meta's AI assistant as well as transcriptions and messages. However, the company has not yet said specifically which features it will support.

Meta introduced Private Processing into WhatsApp and its Meta AI app last year. The service helped enable WhatsApp’s Incognito Chat . The goal was to let customers use AI services without undermining WhatsApp’s flagship end-to-end encrypted secure messaging feature .

In a short conversation at Meta Connect, WIRED spoke with Meta’s Pritam Shah, director of engineering, on adding Private Processing to the glasses.

“What we are doing right now is sharing our excitement about this enhanced privacy platform,” Shah says. “We have the platform ready. We have it working. It's not just a white paper and a blog. The reason why we are announcing it right now, before putting more experiences on this platform, is so that we can start working with the security community and the privacy community and a third-party auditor.”

All of this comes at a moment of reckoning for Meta. The company has long been criticized for how it handles user privacy . This year alone, Meta has fielded months of controversy from people worried about its use of face-recognition technology and how its smart glasses could be used to arm sexual predators . Some people have dubbed them “ pervert glasses ,” confronted people wearing them, and even built apps like ZuckOff to detect Meta’s smart glasses nearby.

More broadly, Meta has been dogged by years of security and privacy gaffes that have eroded user trust, and its products have often seemed to be better at surveilling users than helping them. But at Meta Connect, the company tried to position its smart glasses as a tool that isn’t creepy

When the company launched its Muse AI agent earlier this month, it positioned the assistant as being geared toward security and privacy, specifically touting Muse’s cloud environment, known as Secure VM. It’s working on a version, dubbed Confidential VM, that will feature enhanced privacy guarantees , including a similar promise to make data inaccessible to Meta itself. Muse will also be coming to Meta’s glasses.

Private Processing isn’t available yet on Meta’s glasses, and Shah doesn’t have a timeline for when it will be added or which specific features will work with it.

“These are examples,” he says. “These are not concrete features coming, but these are some examples. And there will be even more powerful examples.”

items.title: Meta is trying VR glasses (again), this time with more IMAX
items.summary: Meta's return to the VR glasses realm comes with a promising combination of light weight form factor and enhanced entertainment options.
items.content:
Meta is renewing its quest to make virtual reality a thing. At Connect on Wednesday, the company announced Meta VR Glasses, its newest entry into the VR market. These glasses actually seem quite promising given their substantially lighter form factor and a host of new entertainment integrations — including (allegedly) IMAX compatibility.

The glasses are largely entertainment-focused and come with micro-OLED panels built into the lenses, which provide a 5K Infinite Display with 37 pixels per degree, as well as Dolby Vision and support for Dolby Atmos audio. Users will be able to download and watch movies.

Perhaps one of the more unique features of the glasses, however, is that Meta is pitching them as a great way to enjoy IMAX-captured films.

Indeed, the company calls the glasses the “first IMAX Enhanced certified VR device ever.” What does that mean? Meta maintains that their glasses will be one of the only ways to experience the expanded aspect ratio that defines the distinct high-resolution viewing experience.

The glasses are also compatible with 3D experiences — and even movies that integrate a user’s physical space is integrated into their viewing experience. Meta says that it has teamed up with Disney and that, in November, Disney+ users will be able to stream specific movies — including certain Marvel movies — in 3D.

Meta says that users will be able to watch specific movies and have their surroundings “transformed with immersive environments, dynamic effects, stunning 3D visuals, and spatial audio” — essentially converting the movie into a VR gaming-type experience.

The glasses will also come with Meta AI — its automated virtual assistant — built in, which means that users will be able to talk to the glasses and automate various tasks via voice command. For instance, Meta says you’ll be able to start a movie just by asking your glasses to do so. Other ways to issue commands include hand gestures.

Meta says the glasses will be available next spring with a starting price of $1299.99.

items.title: Meta VR Glasses, Ray-Ban Meta Audio, Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3: Specs, Features, Prices
items.summary: At its Meta Connect event, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced a handful of new smart glasses, including a slimmed-down VR headset and the company’s first camera-free glasses.
items.content:
After months of controversy about the privacy of its smart glasses , Meta has unveiled the next iteration of its product lineup. At its Meta Connect event in Menlo Park, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced all the new glasses the company is putting out into the world.

Its popular Meta Ray-Ban glasses are now in their third generation, but two new models steal the show: a powerful, slimmed-down version of Meta's Quest headsets capable of virtual and augmented reality modes, and a camera-free pair of Ray-Ban-branded smart glasses, called Ray-Ban Meta Audio. Meta is also bringing its Muse AI agent to its smart glasses platform.

The next evolution of Meta’s Quest VR headset is something truly different. Instead of a heavy helmet-like headset, the new Meta VR Glasses look like big goggles. They’re five times lighter than the Meta Quest 3 . They sit on the nose, right in front of your face like glasses, with no headstrap needed.

They look and feel more like the virtual display glasses made by companies like Viture , and what Xreal’s Project Aura seems to be shaping up to be—lightweight mixed reality lenses that let you access virtual spaces without the burden of a VR headset.

There are no included controllers, though the device can connect to Meta’s previous Quest controllers or gamepads like an Xbox controller. Instead, the wearer controls the device with hand movements and finger pinches, similar to Android XR and Apple’s Vision Pro . Eye tracking pinpoints what you’re trying to access. You can pinch with two fingers to open an app or interact with something on the screen. Form a fist and flick your thumb up or down to scroll the screen.

Inside, the lenses feature a 5K micro-OLED display with a resolution of 2412 x 2288 pixels per eye. The computing power is offloaded to an attached compute puck, which also houses the battery.

Small prescription lens inserts can be magnetically clipped inside the lenses. (Meta has not shared how much those will cost.)

The software is the same that runs on Meta’s Quest VR devices, so movie and game titles in the Quest ecosystem will work on the VR Glasses. That includes games like Beat Saber , live sports apps, and streaming services like Disney+. There are digital workspace modes that let you have multiple monitor screens around you. The VR Glasses can also display a virtual keyboard on a surface in front of you, then use the embedded cameras to track specific finger placements.

The only immediate downside compared to other VR headsets—at least that I could tell from a brief demo at Meta Connect—is that the VR glasses don’t cover your entire field of vision, so it doesn’t feel as immersive as a traditional VR headset.

Meta says the VR Glasses cost $1,300 and will ship in the spring of 2027 .

The Ray-Ban Meta Audio do not have cameras for video or photo capture.

Meta has spent the past few months being absolutely pummeled by controversy about the privacy issues inherent in its camera-enabled smart glasses. The solution? A pair of smart glasses with no cameras.

The Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses have all the audio capabilities of a standard pair of Meta’s smart glasses, minus image and video capture. At 43 grams, they’re also lighter than the others. They have better battery life—12 hours on a single charge and up to 48 hours with the included charging case.

They come in 23 different color and style options, including the retro Ray-Ban Clubmaster frame and a more rectangular Burbank. The Audio glasses cost $349 and are available for preorder now . They start shipping on October 10.

The Meta-branded Gen 3 LISA Adventurer glasses.

Meta's flagship line of smart glasses is getting a “Gen 3” upgrade. They have 12-MP cameras that can capture, like last year, plus 3K Dolby Atmos-enabled video capture. The glasses will get up to 9 hours of battery life, two more than their predecessors. A new six-microphone array offers better sound and can cut out background noise more easily.

A new hearing aid feature called Hearing Enhancement uses the speakers in Meta's glasses to enhance speech and audio around the wearer, similar to the Nuance glasses from EssilorLuxottica .

Earlier this summer, Meta debuted smart glasses under its own branding, which cost a little less but were functionally identical to the Ray-Ban models. Now, it is already following them up with Gen 3 versions. These Meta-branded glasses come in a cat-eye shape called Capri and a rounder lens called Nova.

The Aviator style of the Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3.

The Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses start at $449. Special edition aviator glasses are $579. There are also additional models with colors and styles designed in collaboration with Kylie Jenner and rapper Lisa. (They come with optional charms.) They're available now .

It’s unclear how much the Meta-branded Gen 3 glasses cost. We’ll update this story soon with preorder and sale date information.

Meta's Display glasses are also getting some updates. With the implementation of Meta AI, users can create photorealistic holograms of their faces, which can be helpful for video calls. There are better cycling options and improved navigation apps.

items.title: Meta introduces camera-free AI glasses
items.summary: Meta says the camera-free glasses will be lighter and have up to 12 hours battery life.
items.content:
Confirming earlier reports , Meta announced its first pair of camera-free AI glasses, the clunkily named Ray-Ban Meta Audio, at its Connect 2026 conference on Wednesday. Designed to combat criticism around the more malicious use cases for AI glasses, which saw them nicknamed “pervert glasses” by some, the new devices will be audio-only, offering the ability to listen to music and podcasts, take calls, translate speech, and communicate with Meta’s AI assistant, Muse.

The glasses are designed by Meta’s partner in its AI hardware efforts, EssilorLuxottica, and will start at $349.

While Meta today offers a range of AI glasses in a variety of styles, colors, and capabilities, the audio-only glasses could help the brand recover from some of the reputational damage after critics pointed out how people , often men , were using AI glasses to record videos without subjects’ consent. Meta attempted to mitigate this issue with an update that would disable the camera if the LED light that indicated the glasses were recording was ever tampered with. However, the creepiness factor remained.

This latest device could prove to be more popular for that reason, while also providing an answer to something like Apple’s Siri-powered AirPods.

“Once you get used to high quality audio, it’s just a thing that you want all the time, right?” Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said during a keynote Wednesday, adding that the company after working on the idea realized it could design a whole new category of glasses around audio glasses.

Because they don’t have to house cameras, the glasses are slimmer than Meta’s other models and weigh only 43 grams. They also have adjustable temple tips, swappable nose pads, overextension hinges, and battery life of up to 12 hours on a single charge, Meta claims. With the included charging case, that battery life extends to up to 48 hours.

They’ll also come in a variety of colors and options — 23 color and lens combinations in total — and in two new styles, a retro-inspired “Clubmaster” Ray-Ban style and “Burbank,” described as more of a “classic, timeless, rectangle shape.” Like other Meta glasses, you can order them with your optical prescription as well, if needed.

The glasses will be available for preorder on October 13, the company noted.

Alongside the glasses, Meta announced its next-generation AI glasses (the ones with cameras), the Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 3). In addition to the Ray-Ban Meta Wayfarer, there will also be two new styles, the Aviator and Zena — the latter offering more of a cat-eye frame shape. These will have a 12 MP camera that supports 3K Ultra HD video, a six-mic array, and up to nine hours of battery life.

The glasses Meta launched with EssilorLuxottica will also see an expanded lineup of styles and colors as well as a new partnership with singer Lisa, which follows the company’s earlier brand partnership with Kylie Jenner. The glasses will also be roll out to more countries globally, Meta said.

All of Meta’s AI glasses will, of course, feature access to its newer personal AI assistant, Muse.

The company also teased other coming updates, including support for Dolby Atmos Capture, a feature that picks the best photo from multiple frames, an option to choose landscape or portrait modes, hearing enhancements for those with hearing loss, more detailed responses, different audio modes, customizable controls, and something called “private processing” that Meta claims will prevent the company from seeing your data.

items.title: Meta ditches the camera on its newest smart glasses
items.summary: Walking around Meta Connect 2026, everyone's sporting smart glasses in all sorts of shapes, colors, and sizes. It's a marked difference here, a tech bubble where "pervert glasses" are not a concern. Outside Connect, the public backlash against wearable surveillance tech - a catch
items.content:
Audio-only Ray-Bans have arrived alongside more camera-equipped glasses. What’s missing? Privacy controls to address the ‘perv glasses’ backlash.

Walking around Meta Connect 2026, everyone’s sporting smart glasses in all sorts of shapes, colors, and sizes. It’s a marked difference here, a tech bubble where “pervert glasses” are not a concern.

Outside Connect, the public backlash against wearable surveillance tech — a catchall term that encompasses not just smart glasses, but also smartwatches and AI pendants — is gaining steam. So it’s incredibly curious timing that this year, the company is launching Ray-Ban Meta Audio Glasses: smart glasses infused with Meta AI, but with no camera for recording others.

To hear Meta tell it, that’s a coincidence. Audio-only glasses have been years in the making.

“Three years ago, it wasn’t clear if AI glasses were going to be a thing. Back then, every other company was backing out of the space,” says Alex Himel, Meta’s vice president of wearables. “Then two years ago, we saw that audio was the top use case, the biggest potential for AI, and that it should work well in a pair of audio glasses.”

Himel has a point. Open-ear audio is the least controversial part of the Ray-Bans — and the thing everyone can agree is convenient. Plus, the camera-less glasses are lighter. Himel says that by removing the cameras, Meta could “rearchitect” the glasses. “That allowed us to take a lot of electronics out of the front frame and have a lot more design flexibility.”

The audio-only models start at 43 grams — heavier than normal wire-frame glasses, but noticeably lighter than the roughly 50g Ray-Ban Meta Gen 2 and the 69g Meta Ray-Ban Display . The arms are thinner. They come in two styles: the Mad Men- esque Clubmaster and the more Wayfarer-reminiscent Burbank. The hinges extend for wider faces; the temple arms and nose pads are adjustable. There are 23 color and lens combinations, and they can support the same wider prescription range as the Ray-Ban Meta Optics lineup . Even more so than the standard Meta Ray-Bans, these look and wear like normal glasses. And with a $349 starting price, they’re cheaper too.

Free of a power-hungry camera, the battery lasts an estimated 12 hours on a single charge. The most technical things you can do with them are interact with Meta AI, take phone calls, and listen to podcasts or music. And that’s it.

“They don’t record,” Himel says. “The only thing they do, which is the same thing as an Alexa device in your house or some other devices, they’re just listening for a specific wake word. They’re not sending anything … If they hear [the wake word], then they start listening to what you’re saying. When you’re done talking, then it’s processing, and that’s visible to the AI. It gets processed, and that’s kind of it.”

Slipping them on, they’re comfortable and, I think, quite fetching on me. Regardless of how one might feel about Meta , it’s fair to guess most people would feel less like a creeper wearing these.

I feel differently slipping on the new Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3. Partly because the camera is back in play, partly because the pair Meta gives me is the new aviator style with transition lenses. I’m told I can pull it off, but I keep asking my colleague Jay Peters if I’m giving ’80s serial killer vibes. The other new style is called Zena — not the warrior princess — and it’s a bolder, geometric cat-eye frame.

The third-generation glasses feature fairly minor refinements. There’s a sixth microphone, compared to the second generation’s five, for clearer phone calls. Battery life has gotten a slight boost to nine hours, an hour longer than the second gen. The temple arms, like the audio-only glasses, are adjustable for a better fit. All sound will now be captured in Dolby Atmos for spatial audio. Sure! That’s neat if I’m in my quiet hotel room, but it’s harder to appreciate when reviewing footage amid the hustle and bustle of Meta Connect. The new model comes in 27 color and lens combinations, plus three seasonal options.

Along with the hardware changes, the Gen 3 glasses are also getting a price bump. They start at $449, up from $379 for the second-gen models last year.

Meta Glasses — the off-brand, more affordable entry-level glasses launched a few months ago — also have more options. There are two new styles, Capri and Nova. Capri is some kind of cat-eye shape, while Nova… honestly, the styles are all starting to blur together. They’re round and remind me of several other Ray-Ban Meta glasses, but slightly different. There’s a new ivory-colored Kylie Jenner pair that costs $399.

But maybe Kylie Jenner isn’t the celebrity collab you’ve been dreaming about. That’s fine. Because Blackpink’s Lisa — a K-pop icon and The White Lotus actress — also has Meta Glasses. They have pink lenses and come with a blind-box-type charm styled after Lisa’s pets. These also start at $399. (Non-celebrity versions of the Meta Glasses start at $249.)

Why the celebrity collabs? Options for more people, including women.

“With the Meta Glasses Starfire with Kylie, we saw a younger, more female audience start to buy the glasses,” says Himel. “Wayfarer is the most popular glasses type in the world, but it tends to be more male — though definitely not exclusively male. The second brand we did was Oakley … but Oakley [also] tends to be a more masculine brand. So I think with Kylie and Lisa, and with more styles, we’re seeing them appeal to more women.”

There are actually more limited-edition versions, styles, colors, and prescription permutations available across the entire existing Ray-Ban Meta lineup at a whole range of price points. I suspect I’d need to make a spreadsheet to list them all. While scuttling about Meta’s campus this week, I’m brought to an entire area where they’re all displayed. It looks like a high-end store for, regular, schmegular glasses. That, I suspect, is the whole point.

items.title: Vogue sent robots down the runway at Vogue World, and people were not impressed
items.summary: Nothing says Italian craftsmanship like a Chinese robot doing a lasso to "L'Amour Toujours."
items.content:
Vogue World closed its Milan edition this week with a troupe of robots — perhaps a preview of what’s coming when the event descends on San Francisco next year.

Vogue World is the magazine’s annual traveling spectacle, now in its fifth year: part runway show, part celebrity showcase, part variety hour, part ad-sales opportunity , staged in a different city each time. It has run through New York, London, Paris, and Hollywood. This year’s Milan edition was marketed as a tribute to Italian craftsmanship and “the human touch” in an age of technology, which makes what happened next a little strange.

During the act titled The Age of Intelligence, humanoid robots made by the Chinese firm Unitree walked into the Galleria to Gigi D’Agostino’s “L’Amour Toujours.” They waved their arms in the air, imploring onlookers to clap. One did a lasso. They were not wearing clothes. The pained expression of Alessandro Michele, the creative director of Valentino, quickly went viral.

Vogue World Milano ends (appropriately Europoor-kitschily) with tiny robottini dancing to L’Amour Toujours while Alessandro Michele slowly dies inside pic.twitter.com/xicYWWl6VW

I haven’t seen a single thing about the actual fashion that was presented at Vogue World Milan. Instead, everyone is talking about the robots. (These same robots have been making headlines worldwide for their dance moves , and for falling and breaking .) Similar robots turned up on the runway at London Fashion Week, which is happening now.

Vogue turned heads earlier this year when it announced that the next edition will be in San Francisco, arguably one of the least stylish cities in the United States. The timing isn’t coincidental. Anna Wintour has aligned herself ever more closely with the tech barons of our time, and Vogue World Milan was itself sponsored in part by Meta Glasses, with additional support from OpenAI.

It was one of those moments that reveals how thoroughly tech exists in a bubble, and that not everyone is happy with the rapid adoption of new technology, or by Vogue cozying up to the symbols of the insanely rich — and only getting richer — tech titans during a cost-of-living crisis. That’s before you get to AI, mass surveillance, the displacement of labor, and the energy crisis, all of them overseen by the same titans. For some, a robot on a runway is further proof of what is going wrong in the world right now.

miuccia prada when the fuckass robot walked out during vogue world pic.twitter.com/SebwpV0zkl

We are all Alessandro Michele, sitting front row at Vogue World Milan, having an existential crisis about the absolute state of things while robots awkwardly dance about. Numb to the pain at this point. Madness.

just got off the phone with the creative director of Vogue World. First question he asked me. “So you hated the robots?” 🤭 Full interview on Substack tomorrow 👀 https://t.co/FTa3gumPgY

“I’m annoyed by the celebrities cheering the whole thing,” one tech founder wrote me on Instagram. “It’s sick and gloom. People are literally losing jobs and livelihoods because of these things. They need to stop encouraging it. What’s it even modeling? Headphones?”

One fashion reporter friend simply said “No,” when I asked for thoughts on the robots and Vogue World San Francisco. Jason Johnson, founder of Culture Impact Agency, noted that Vogue has been trying to build a relationship with Silicon Valley for at least the past decade, highlighting when Jony Ive co-hosted the Met Gala back in 2015. The dancing robots at Vogue World Milan were inevitable, then, as is Vogue World San Francisco and as was Jeff Bezos and his wife, Lauren Sanchez, getting the splashy Vogue wedding cover and co-hosting the 2026 Met Gala.

“Publications are figuring out new ways to make money and tech has money,” he told me. “Vogue has the cultural influence and access that those tech people want.” Both sides win in the end, he said.

Still, something about the way Vogue is going about this feels unnatural.

Muna Ikedionwu, founder of MKEDI, a strategy firm for early-stage startups, said what she found most interesting about the robots is that they don’t fully represent the innovation and progress that’s actually happening in the creative technologist space. “I’ve seen such incredible examples of engineering and AI being used to influence fashion, being used to influence design and art,” she told me, adding that robots walking down the runway doesn’t even scratch the surface of what is happening right now at the intersection of fashion and tech.

She points to the artist duo AA Murakami , who created Olympian Eileen Gu’s dress of bubbles at this year’s Met Gala . They are fashion designers but also engineers, Ikedionwu said, noting a presentation she saw them give recently about how to create an “everlasting bubble.” They are helping to pioneer “emphemeral technology,” she said, “this idea of technology and innovation that speaks to the ephemeral nature or the temporariness of art and humanity and the soul.”

Sure, I guess when you compare it to this, the robots did seem quite boring. Whenever I think about the intersection of fashion and technology, I think about that Spring 2024 Schiaparelli collection , which unveiled a robot baby crafted with Swarovski crystals and a dress made with vintage tech like PC microchips. (I once threatened to wear that dress to Disrupt; see image above.)

Ikedionwu wonders whether this robot performance was a way to make the general public more comfortable with technology and fashion overlapping, a merger that has been underway behind the scenes for years. If so, it didn’t work. But maybe Vogue World is saving all the good stuff for San Francisco.

items.title: Meta is making Muse more powerful and will let you video chat with it, too
items.summary: Meta is quickly iterating on its new Muse AI agent, announcing a bunch of updates today that make the bot more capable and able to chat with you in more ways. Muse agents are getting their own email addresses that they can use for accomplishing tasks. You'll also be able to commu
items.content:
Muse started as a chatbot but will soon be an AI avatar you can talk with over video.

Meta is quickly iterating on its new Muse AI agent, announcing a bunch of updates today that make the bot more capable and able to chat with you in more ways.

Muse agents are getting their own email addresses that they can use for accomplishing tasks. You’ll also be able to communicate with your Muse agent over the new email addresses, too. In addition, the recently launched Muse Mac app will be getting the ability to use your computer.

Meta is also going to give you another way to chat with its popular AI agent: video calls. Since its recent launch, the primary way to talk with Muse was through a chat interface, but you’ll soon be able to have live video conversations with your Muse avatar. Meta will let you tweak the way your Muse avatar sounds — you can already customize the way it looks — and a new Muse Realtime Avatar model will inform how it moves.

Muse launched earlier this month , and it’s seemingly proving to be a hit, topping the App Store charts and reportedly being downloaded more than ChatGPT on mobile in its first 12 days. Meta appears to be capitalizing on the popularity by quickly introducing the new videocalling features, but that’s not all that’s new for the agent. Meta says it plans to launch Muse on its smart glasses in the coming months, which will let you talk to Muse about what you’re looking at while wearing your glasses.

items.content:
It’s about time for Meta Connect, the company’s annual product launch event. This year, given the company’s major focus on AI and wearables like smart glasses, it seems likely that we’ll see updates from CEO Mark Zuckerberg and his team on those categories. The company has been facing significant scrutiny because of how some users have been covertly recording other people using the glasses, meaning that one of the biggest announcements of the show could be its rumored camera-free pair .

Connect has also traditionally been a venue for updates on Meta’s VR hardware and software. While the company has scaled back its VR ambitions, a recent leak seemingly revealing some kind of unannounced mixed reality glasses could indicate that Meta will show off new immersive headwear technology during the event.

Zuckerberg’s keynote is scheduled to begin at 7PM ET / 4PM PT on Wednesday, September 23rd. Follow along with all of our coverage right here.

Meta announced a slate of new wearables during its annual Meta Connect showcase on Wednesday. The star of the event was the new Meta VR Glasses, which pack virtual reality tech into a lightweight smart glasses-style frame with a tethered puck. Meta also announced new pairs of screen-free smart glasses, along with some new AI features and style and frame options.

You can catch up on all the highlights from this year’s Meta Connect below.

Meta is promising that “hundreds” of movies will be available “later this year” in the US, with “thousands of titles available internationally” when the new Meta VR Glasses launch in spring 2027.

Meta is launching new VR hardware: a pair of glasses. The new Meta VR Glasses sit on your ears like a typical pair of glasses instead of being strapped over your head, but they still have immersive displays for watching movies, playing games, and getting work done. Imagine a pair of hefty black sunglasses with blacked-out lenses on the outside, but the components of a typical VR headset distributed between the device on your head and a computing puck in your pocket.

The idea is to give you a way to experience VR in a much lighter and more approachable form factor than Vision Pro or Meta Quest-style headsets. I got to try the VR Glasses at Meta’s campus this week, and as Meta walked me through some familiar VR demos like watching content, playing a game, and working from multiple screens, I was impressed by how much lighter the whole experience felt. Some of that was about the literal weight, as the glasses come in at just 100g, far less than the Quest 3’s 515g. But there was also something lighter in a more intangible way: the glasses form factor made the headset seem like something I could easily jump in and out of instead of being a whole cumbersome commitment with big head straps. It felt like a lightweight Vision Pro, and is perhaps a better execution of some of what Apple wanted to do with that device.

Just a couple of weeks after launching Muse , Meta announced that it’s “working on” bringing the agent to its smart glasses, including the new glasses it unveiled at Meta Connect. Users will be able to activate Muse from their glasses by saying its name and ask it to handle tasks like guiding a workout, logging meals, or helping them shop for products they’re looking at.

Muse is just one of several major updates coming to Meta’s glasses. They’re also getting some new accessibility features, like a Hearing Enhancement feature Meta says is “FDA-cleared software for adults with perceived mild to moderate hearing loss.” It will be available later this year with a Meta One subscription or as a $149 add-on for compatible glasses. Meta AI will also be able to give “more context-rich answers” when users ask the glasses what they’re looking at, potentially making Meta’s glasses more effective for helping blind and low-vision users interpret their surroundings. A new audio customization feature will also allow users to shift their smart glasses’ volume between their left and right ears, including sending all audio to one side.

Walking around Meta Connect 2026, everyone’s sporting smart glasses in all sorts of shapes, colors, and sizes. It’s a marked difference here, a tech bubble where “pervert glasses” are not a concern.

Outside Connect, the public backlash against wearable surveillance tech — a catchall term that encompasses not just smart glasses, but also smartwatches and AI pendants — is gaining steam. So it’s incredibly curious timing that this year, the company is launching Ray-Ban Meta Audio Glasses: smart glasses infused with Meta AI, but with no camera for recording others.

Meta is quickly iterating on its new Muse AI agent, announcing a bunch of updates today that make the bot more capable and able to chat with you in more ways.

Muse agents are getting their own email addresses that they can use for accomplishing tasks. You’ll also be able to communicate with your Muse agent over the new email addresses, too. In addition, the recently launched Muse Mac app will be getting the ability to use your computer.

Meta says that today’s keynote by Mark Zuckerberg will be about how “Meta is building a future for everyone” — something he wrote at length about in a recent essay about AI, smart glasses, and more. That means we can expect more news from Zuckerberg and his team on those topics; perhaps we’ll hear more about Meta’s recently launched Muse AI agent and new glasses hardware.

items.title: Anthropic says its biology lab has already found something big
items.summary: But maybe the biggest reveal is that Anthropic has not let Claude run loose in its biology lab. Humans are still, so far, in the loop.
items.content:
Last week, Anthropic confirmed that it was operating a wet biology lab in the Bay Area where it uses its AI models to run physical experiments. This week, the AI giant announced that this lab has already made what it believes is a big discovery: a new enzyme “system” that has certain “properties reminiscent of CRISPR,” as Anthropic describes it .

CRISPR is a natural immune system used by bacteria to fight off viruses that has become a gene-editing technology widely used by researchers .

Essentially, what Anthropic says it found is a previously unknown enzyme system hidden in the DNA of bacteriophages, which are viruses that infect and replicate within bacteria. Anthropic’s researchers say this system behaves similarly to CRISPR in that it can “perform operations like cutting, copying, and pasting DNA.”

It will be up to the broader research community to validate how big, or new, this discovery actually is. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei acknowledges that the discovery was based on the work of others and that a team from Stanford previously discovered a system “that is in some ways similar to the one Claude found,” he wrote on X .

But Amodei and Anthropic are not just emphasizing the discovery. They are touting it was found “mostly, though not entirely, by Claude,” the CEO wrote.

On the one hand, that is astounding. This lab was only established this spring (though Anthropic declined to be more specific about how many months it has been open). A discovery in just a few short months would be speedy enough work, but the team said it actually only took Claude 21 hours of concerted effort. Claude searched through data using about 950 agents that burned through 210 million tokens.

Still, the revelation that Anthropic has been conducting biology experiments comes right after AI CEOs, including Amodei , publicly admitted that models have become so capable, and so potentially dangerous, that the industry must slow down and develop safety-testing procedures. This after a couple of his employees publicly said earlier this month that there’s a risk AI could kill us all .

Amodei himself has said one of the things he fears most is that AI could be used for bioterrorism. But he also believes AI will “cure most diseases in 5-10 years,” he wrote. So Anthropic has clearly decided the rewards are worth the risks.

Given that, perhaps the biggest reveal in this news isn’t the discovery itself but that the biology lab hasn’t let Claude loose. The physical experiments were done by humans.

“Our lab, located in the Bay Area, looks like a typical molecular biology lab. We do research that involves only the lower-levels of the biosafety risk level (BSL-1 and BSL-2) and we do not handle pathogens that can infect humans. All of the lab work is performed by human scientists.”

It’s also true that AI-powered biological research is hardly unique to Anthropic. Researchers from Stanford just published a paper on the work they are doing with LLMs and CRISPR. Researchers at UC San Francisco used AI to design enzymes from scratch . Google launched its first AI-powered biology research tool, AlphaFold, back in 2020 . So AI has clearly arrived in biological research beyond the AI labs pursuing it themselves.

Yet, Amodei hasn’t ruled out a fully automated biology lab in the future. “Eventually it may even be possible for Claude itself to safely perform the experiments by autonomously controlling lab equipment, with appropriate safeguards in place, but we aren’t doing that today,” he said.

items.content:
AI 에이전트라는 말이 등장한 지는 벌써 2~3년이 됐습니다. 하지만 최근 들어서야 일반 사용자들이 체감할 만한 서비스가 나오기 시작했습니다. 스페이스XAI의 ‘그록봇(Grok Bot)’ 은 출시 한 달 만에 이용자 40만명 이상을 확보했고, 메타의 개인용 에이전트 ‘뮤즈(Muse)’ 도 출시 첫 주 50만명 이상의 사용자를 확보한 것으로 알려졌습니다.

아직 이 수치만으로 에이전트가 대중화됐다고 보기는 어렵습니다. 다만 그동안 기업이나 개발자의 생산성 도구에 가까웠던 AI 에이전트가 일반 소비자의 일상으로 영역을 넓히기 시작했다는 점은 눈여겨볼 만합니다.

그록봇과 뮤즈가 주목받는 이유도 여기에 있습니다.

그록봇은 이메일 답장이나 데이터 정리, 송장 처리 같은 반복적인 업무를 대신하는 데 초점을 맞추고 있습니다. 테슬라 차량에도 탑재 돼 운전자가 음성으로 AI에게 작업을 지시할 수 있도록 했습니다.

뮤즈는 범위가 더 일상적입니다. 이메일을 보내고, 여행을 예약하고, 온라인 쇼핑을 하고, 필요한 경우 전화를 걸어 업체와 대화하는 식입니다. 메타는 사용자가 일일이 과정을 지시하지 않아도 목표를 전달하면 여러 단계를 거쳐 작업을 수행하도록 뮤즈를 설계했습니다.

결국 두 서비스가 보여주는 것은 ‘AI가 더 똑똑해졌다’는 것만은 아닙니다. AI를 쓰는 이유가 ‘내 일을 더 잘하기 위해서’에서 ‘내가 하기 귀찮은 일을 대신 시키기 위해서’로 넓어지고 있다는 것입니다.

그동안 AI 에이전트의 대표적인 활용 사례는 코딩, 문서 작성, 자료 조사처럼 생산성과 직접 연결되는 일이었습니다. 오픈AI의 '챗GPT 워크'나 앤트로픽의 '클로드 코워크'도 이런 흐름에서 발전했습니다.

하지만 일반 소비자에게는 꼭 거창한 업무가 필요한 것은 아닙니다. 이메일에 답장을 보내거나, 식당에 전화를 걸거나, 여행 일정을 정리하거나, 필요한 물건을 찾아 구매하는 것처럼 매일 반복되지만 직접 하기는 귀찮은 일이 더 쉽게 와닿을 수 있습니다.

이런 의미에서 오래전부터 이야기해 온 ‘AI 개인 비서’라는 개념도 이제 조금씩 구체적인 모습을 갖추기 시작한 셈입니다.

개인 비서라면 결국 사용자의 말을 듣고 정보를 알려주는 것만으로는 부족합니다. 사용자를 대신해 일을 처리해야 합니다. 그것도 한 번에 끝나는 질문에 답하는 것이 아니라 반복적이고 번거로운 일을 맡아 처리하는 쪽에 가깝습니다.

기술적으로도 이런 변화가 가능해질 조건이 갖춰지고 있습니다. 최근 에이전트는 단순히 문장을 생성하는 데 그치지 않고 브라우저와 앱을 직접 조작하고, 외부 도구를 사용하고, 여러 단계를 이어서 실행합니다. 장시간 작업을 유지하는 실행 환경과 사용자의 맥락을 기억하는 기능까지 더해지면서 ‘대화하는 AI’에서 ‘행동하는 AI’로 역할이 넓어지고 있습니다.

올해 초 개발자와 AI 파워유저 사이에서 주목받은 '오픈클로(OpenClaw)'가 보여준 것도 바로 이런 가능성이었습니다. AI와 대화하는 것을 넘어 실제 컴퓨터 환경에서 일을 시키는 방식입니다. 메타는 뮤즈 개발 과정에서 오픈클로의 영향 을 받았다는 점도 인정했습니다.

구글도 이미 움직이고 있습니다. 지난 5월 ‘제미나이 스파크’를 공개하며 지메일과 문서·프레젠테이션 등 구글 워크스페이스와 연동해 사용자의 작업을 대신 수행하는 에이전트 기능을 선보였습니다.

따라서 구글과 오픈AI가 뒤처졌다고 해석하기는 어렵습니다. 오히려 이제부터는 비슷한 기술을 가진 기업들이 어떤 구체적인 사용 사례로 사람들을 끌어들이느냐가 중요해질 가능성이 큽니다.

실제로 오픈AI는 그록봇과 뮤즈의 초기 반응에 주목, 이에 대응하기 위한 기능을 준비하고 있는 것으로 알려졌습니다. 챗GPT가 이미 웹 작업을 대신 수행하는 기능을 갖추고 있는 만큼, 앞으로는 이를 일반 소비자가 매일 사용할 만한 개인 비서 형태로 얼마나 확장하느냐가 관건이 될 수 있습니다.

물론 아직 갈 길은 멉니다. 이메일이나 쇼핑, 예약처럼 실제 행동을 맡기려면 AI가 틀리지 않는 것뿐 아니라 어떤 정보에 접근할 수 있고 어디까지 행동할 수 있는지를 통제해야 합니다. 메타가 뮤즈의 전화 기능에서 일부 통화를 사람이 대신 처리하는 ‘ 휴먼 컨시어지 ’를 테스트하고 있다는 사실도 아직 에이전트가 모든 일을 완전히 자동화하기에는 해결해야 할 문제가 있다는 것을 보여줍니다.

결국 지금은 ‘AI 에이전트 시대가 열렸다’고 선언할 단계라기보다 에이전트가 어떤 모습이어야 사람들이 실제로 쓰는지를 찾아가는 초기 단계에 가깝습니다.

앞으로 시장을 주도할 핵심도 에이전트라는 기술 용어 자체가 아니라, “AI가 나 대신 무엇을 해줄 수 있는가”라는 질문에 얼마나 명확하고 구체적인 유즈 케이스를 제공하느냐에 달려 있습니다.

그동안 AI 에이전트가 주로 기업의 생산성을 높이는 기술로 설명됐다면, 이제는 방향이 조금 달라지고 있습니다. 일을 더 많이 하게 만드는 AI가 아니라, 하기 싫고 귀찮은 일을 대신 해주는 AI가 개인 비서에 가까워지는 진정한 이유인 셈입니다.

■ 오픈AI, 'GPT-6 솔·루나' 공개…"필요한 성능만 올리고 가격은 반값"

오픈AI는 이제 아티피셜 인텔리전스의 종합 순위 경쟁보다 필요한 기능을 강화하고 비용을 낮추는 데 무게를 두는 모습입니다. 코딩과 에이전트 작업 성능을 끌어올리면서 가격은 기존 모델 대비 절반으로 낮춰, 경쟁력을 확보하려는 전략이 두드러집니다.

■ 새로운 최고 성능·가격 40% 인하…앤트로픽, '클로드 오퍼스 5.5' 공개

앤트로픽은 최근 공개한 모델들이 잇따라 아티피셜 인텔리전스에서 최고 성능을 기록하고 있지만, 여전히 비용 경쟁력에서는 과제가 남아 있습니다. 이번 모델도 API 운영 비용을 40% 낮췄지만, 오픈AI가 솔·루나의 가격을 절반으로 낮추면서 비용 경쟁에서는 다시 격차가 벌어지는 모습입니다.

■ 샤오미, 오픈 모델 ‘미모-V2.6’ 공개…중국 AI 중 역대 최고 성적

반년 가까이 잠잠했던 샤오미가 새 모델을 내놓으며 다시 중국 오픈 모델 경쟁의 선두로 올라섰습니다. 이제는 딥시크와 알리바바, 지푸AI, 문샷AI에 이어 빼놓기 어려운 주요 기업으로 자리 잡는 모습입니다.

트레이더들은 위험 노출을 관리하면서 방대한 시장 데이터를 이해하느라 애를 먹을 때가 많다. FXT AI는 트레이더의 기존 계정 안에서 전문 에이전트 세 가지가 긴밀하게 협업하는 방식으로 이러한 문제를 해결한다. 새 앱을 따로 다운로드 받을 필요가 없다. 트레이더는 대시보드를 열기만 하면 즉시 실행 가능한 인사이트를 얻을 수 있으며, 질문을 통해 시장 움직임과 개인 거래 성과를 더욱 심층적으로 파악할 수 있다.

FXT AI는 일반적인 시장 신호와 달리 트레이더의 실제 계정 활동을 기반으로 구축됐다. 모든 인사이트는 투명하며 그 근거를 설명할 수 있다. FXT AI는 전략 수립에 필요한 정보를 제공하지만, 거래 여부를 결정하고 실제 거래를 실행하는 주체는 항상 트레이더다.

애덤 필립스(Adam Phillips) FXT 최고경영자는 "우리는 트레이더의 습관과 시장을 더 폭넓게 이해하는 파트너를 제공하고자 FXT AI를 구축했다"며 "FXT AI는 복잡성을 명확한 개인 맞춤 인사이트로 전환해 고객이 기회를 파악하고 거래 프로세스를 강화하며 자신 있게 의사결정을 내릴 수 있도록 지원한다"고 말했다.

FXT AI는 웹, 데스크톱, 모바일 기기 전반에서 FXT 플랫폼을 통해 직접 구동되며, MT4와 MT5 등 타사 MetaQuotes 플랫폼과 함께 사용할 수 있다. FXT는 플랫폼 기능을 지속적으로 확장하고 있으며, 현재 추가 전문 에이전트도 개발 중이다.

FXT는 글렌이글 그룹(Gleneagle Group) 소속으로, 기업 자문, 펀드 운용, 기관 거래, 브로커리지 및 트레이딩 플랫폼 서비스를 제공하며 금융시장 발전을 선도하고 있다. 호주 금융서비스 라이선스(Australian Financial Services License)와 바누아투 금융서비스위원회(Vanuatu Financial Services Commission, VFSC) 금융 라이선스를 보유하고 있다. FXT는 계정 하나로 외환(FX), 지수, 원자재 및 주식 등 200여 가지 상품에 접근할 수 있는 멀티에셋 차액결제거래(CFD) 플랫폼이다.

items.title: A US-China AI Hotline Won't Be Ready For a While
items.summary: As the US and China race to become the dominant power in the AI industry, the countries also appear to be figuring out ways to communicate on national security issues.
items.content:
As US president Donald Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping prepare to meet in Washington for a state dinner at the White House on Thursday, AI has become a top priority . Tech executives from OpenAI and Nvidia have confirmed their attendance at the dinner, as a number of key agenda items are on the table.

Chief among them is a US proposal to establish an AI notification system with China, akin to the Cold War hotline with Moscow, which would allow each country to alert the other about national security issues related to AI. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent first announced the notification system on Sunday with Chinese vice premier He Lifeng.

But for all the high-level progress, Trump administration officials tell Inner Loop they expect it to still take a number of weeks to finalize an agreement, even if they are optimistic that the hotline could be in place before the year’s end.

There are several parts that need to be formalized in more detail, including establishing benchmarks on what kind of incident rises to the level of a national security issue, which remains unclear, as well as explicit sign-on from China, which has been noncommittal.

Trump officials tell Inner Loop they are essentially targeting a framework for the system to be functional—and, crucially, agreed to by Trump—by the time Bessent next meets with Lifeng in follow-up talks in two months' time in Shenzhen, China.

The discussions around such a mechanism underscore the growing concern around the rapidly developing capabilities of frontier AI models as the US and China race to become the dominant power in the industry.

Trump officials have internally discussed putting together a framework that lays out criteria for when each country is obligated to alert the other and enforcement measures to ensure it doesn't only become the US alerting the Chinese.

But with the US expected to extend a trade truce and Trump reluctant to stop exports of cutting-edge Nvidia chips to China, developing a framework that has enforcement measures with teeth could take time to get White House approval, sources say.

The administration has granted a limited number of licenses this year for Nvidia to sell its H200 chip to China, a critical component for AI labs to increase compute power to train their models. Nvidia’s supporters have argued that not selling the chips incentivizes Chinese companies like Huawei to develop their own chip technology, though according to recent reports, the company has already achieved that milestone with its commercially available AI chips.

Some Trump officials have also suggested the notification system may also be delayed while Trump decides on who to appoint as his next "AI czar” to lead a so-called "AI Force," which is being envisioned as a role in charge of interagency coordination.

Bessent has been one of the names floated as the AI czar, but it is not clear if he’s the standout. Commerce secretary Howard Lutnick and White House AI officials Michael Kratsios and Sean Cairncross are also in the mix , two sources tell Inner Loop.

It remains unclear if Trump will choose someone who will be wearing two hats or is departing their current role to take the position. The previous AI czar, David Sacks, was in the position as a special government employee. Sacks is not considered to be in the mix to return, the sources say.

The push for Bessent has come in part because the AI notification system is seen as something akin to the US-China dialogue between former Treasury secretary Hank Paulson and former Chinese vice premier of finance Wang Qishan. During the 2008 financial crisis, Paulson credited the hotline as helping to stave off China from dumping a large portion of US government sponsored debt issued by Freddie Mac and Fannie Mae.

Meanwhile, while some Trump officials have chafed at the idea of giving more AI power to Lutnick, he remains in contention insofar as he oversees the Center for AI Standards and Innovation, which successfully navigated crises with frontier AI model companies this summer.

items.title: Trump’s China rivalry and “AI race” delusion may endanger US, experts say
items.summary: Trump focus on winning “AI race” may deter China from sharing safety intel.
items.content:
This week, the US and China, the two world leaders on AI, finally started talks meant to keep the whole world safe from emerging safety risks. But whether meetings between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping can lead to a reliable global governance framework for AI depends on how much the fierce rivals are actually willing to cooperate.

It’s clear Trump wants it to seem like discussions are going well. Before Trump and Xi meet on Thursday and Friday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that both sides had already discussed setting up a new AI safety notification mechanism. If China agrees to participate, that would create an open line for either side to send alerts when their country’s AI systems pose threats or behave unpredictably. The same channel, Bessent said, could allow the countries to share their “vision of common goals.”

However, the proposal comes at a time when China may not be ready to trust the US to have AI safety conversations that aren’t about limiting China’s capabilities. Not only has Trump steadily increased export controls that explicitly seek to block China from accessing technology to advance AI, but Congress is mulling bills that would cut the country off from more chips and hardware. Adding to tensions, just two weeks ago, Trump’s Justice Department accused six of China’s leading AI makers of stealing from US frontier labs, which China has strongly disputed.

Some US-China experts told Ars that there were concerns that China might cancel talks, but China seemingly isn’t taking offense to Trump’s rhetoric. Even Truth Social posts where Trump insists that America must dominate China on AI—declaring “WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so”—didn’t keep China from showing up.

Notably, China has yet to publicly acknowledge the proposed alert system. Even if China bought into the system, people familiar with Bessent’s plan told Politico that the plan to monitor safety alerts appears superficial, since it involves no officials with technical expertise who could be trusted to assess the urgency of risks described in communications.

Describing the significance of the arrangement, one source mocked the plan, saying “the scientific, technical term is BS.”

Sam Bresnick, a research fellow at a Georgetown University think tank called the Center for Security and Emerging Technology, monitors national security applications of AI and US-China tech competition. He agreed it’s a red flag that there’s no tech body of tech experts monitoring the channel.

“It’s an existing channel, which I think is better than creating a whole new channel,” Bresnick told Ars. But if both sides had tech experts, the US and China could have really high-level conversations about how they’re assessing risk. That’s particularly important when discussing military risks, Bresnick emphasized.

“I think it’s better than nothing for sure, but I don’t have a lot of confidence that that is going to make a major difference going forward,” Bresnick said.

Su Lian Jye, a chief analyst at a global technology research and advisory group called Omdia, told the South China Morning Post that the AI alerts may help “promote more transparency,” but it won’t make either side less wary of the other.

“I don’t think the dialog will remove all concerns and differences on distillation, pricing competition, and pacing,” Su said.

Praising the plan as a good start to open dialogues, Su suggested that much more cooperation would be needed to make the safety mechanism meaningful.

“Turning the proposal into an effective tool would require both countries to agree on risk classifications, notification triggers, response protocols, and regular review procedures,” he said.

Perhaps that will come up when Trump and Xi meet later this week, with AI supposedly at the top of the agenda.

It’s unclear what will be discussed, but critics concerned about the most urgent AI safety risks fear that Bessent’s announcement indicates that Trump has modest ambitions for the summit.

On CBS’s “Face the Nation,” US Representative Ro Khanna—the ranking Democrat on the US House Select Committee on ⁠Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party—suggested that talks between Trump and Xi should go much further than setting up a line between two officials with no tech expertise.

He argued Trump should be asking Xi for an international agreement that urgently includes “banning any recursive self-improving AI” and “safeguards so that AI can’t be misused by people for biological nuclear weapons.”

Many experts described sharing safety alerts as a decent first step in improving US-China coordination on AI, which Trump’s incoming “AI czar” could then possibly build on.

Alvin Wang Graylin, a global technology strategist and digital fellow at Stanford Digital Economy Lab, has spent decades weighing geopolitical risks. Most recently, he’s advised governments and tech leaders on AI policy and global governance, including sharing recommendations on how to set up a notification system like the one Bessent proposed.

Graylin told Ars that he was surprised to see that such a “positive” development had already come out of this week’s talks with China. And it seemed encouraging that both countries already have another meeting scheduled in November.

“What that shows is that both sides are seeing value in the discussion,” Graylin said. “Otherwise, there would not be a follow-on.”

Graylin suggested the US and China share many AI risks. Not just the supposedly existential risk that AI leaders started recently claiming required a slowdown , but also risks from bad actors like hackers or terrorists wielding AI to attack either country’s infrastructure.

[스냅드래곤 서밋 2026] AI 성능 2배·초저전력 와이파이 통합…오디오·비전 결합 폼팩터

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/09/24 05:42 수정: 2026/09/24 08:28

[마우이(미국)=지디넷코리아 전화평 기자] 무선 이어폰 등 오디오 웨어러블 기기가 단순히 소리를 듣는 도구를 넘어, 사용자 상황을 인지하고 대화형으로 돕는 '인공지능(AI) 비서'로 탈바꿈한다.

퀄컴은 24일(현지시간) 미국 하와이 마우이에서 열린 '스냅드래곤 서밋 2026'에서 차세대 지능형 오디오 기기용 '스냅드래곤 사운드 엘리트 2세대 플랫폼'을 공개했다. 신규 플랫폼은 프리미엄 오디오 기술에 강력한 온디바이스 AI, 클라우드 연동 AI, 초저전력 와이파이(Wi-Fi) 6E를 하나로 통합해 직관적이고 개인화된 오디오 경험을 구현하는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

가장 눈에 띄는 변화는 효율성이다. 전작 대비 AI 연산 성능을 최대 2배 끌어올려 기기 자체에서 여러 지능형 기능을 매끄럽게 실행하면서도, 전력 소비는 최대 40%, 칩 면적은 최대 30% 줄였다. 배터리 제약 없이 언제든 즉각 반응하는 퍼스널 AI 기기 설계가 가능해졌다. 퀄컴은 이 플랫폼이 카메라를 탑재해 사진 촬영 대신 사용자 주변 맥락을 파악하는 새로운 형태 폼팩터에도 적용할 수 있다고 설명했다.

지아드 아스가르 퀄컴 수석 부사장 겸 XR(확장현실)·웨어러블·퍼스널 AI 본부장은 "자체 조사에서 사용자의 최대 70%가 웨어러블 기기에 첨단 AI 기능 탑재를 원한다"며 "AI가 일상화될수록 항상 화면을 보는 방식이 아닌, AI 비서에게 직접 말을 걸고 실시간으로 도움을 받는 자연스러운 음성 상호작용이 중요해질 것"이라고 강조했다.

이어 "새 플랫폼은 실시간 번역, 맥락 기반 어시스턴트, 오디오와 비전을 결합한 멀티모달 상호작용 등 새로운 가능성을 열고 있다"고 덧붙였다.

연결성과 오디오 본연 성능도 강화됐다. 초저전력 와이파이 6E를 활용하는 '스냅드래곤 사운드 앱스 앤 에이전트'는 스마트폰을 거치지 않고 오디오 기기가 클라우드에 직접 연결되도록 돕는다. '퀄컴 aptX 로스리스'로 고음질을 구현하고, '퀄컴 XPAN'을 통해 기존 블루투스 한계를 뛰어넘는 끊김 없는 연결을 지원한다.

또한 5세대 퀄컴 액티브노이즈캔슬링(ANC)과 다중 마이크 아키텍처를 바탕으로 소음 환경에서도 또렷한 대화와 안정적인 음성인식을 제공한다. '스냅드래곤 오디오 센스 솔루션'은 사람 목소리와 주변 소리를 명확히 구분해 AI가 빠르고 정확하게 반응하도록 돕는다.

퀄컴은 이 플랫폼이 이어버드, 헤드폰은 물론 오디오 글래스와 미래 멀티모달 웨어러블 등 다양한 폼팩터로 확장될 것이라고 내다봤다. 글로벌 오디오 브랜드 클리어(Cleer)는 이번 행사에서 해당 플랫폼을 기반으로 오디오와 비전, AI를 결합한 새로운 개념의 지능형 오디오 웨어러블 시제품을 시연해 차세대 기기 청사진을 제시했다.

items.title: VC firm Bessemer now has another $5.75B to invest in (what else?) AI
items.summary: The VC firm says that AI-native companies are growing faster than any technology, ever.
items.content:
Bessemer Venture Partners announced on Wednesday that it has raised $5.75 billion across two new funds to accelerate its investment across all parts of the AI stack. The firm, which has backed companies such as Anthropic, Cognition, Legora, Perplexity, Ramp, Shopify, and Waymo, dedicated $1.75 billion for seed and early-stage investing and the remaining $4 billion for growth startups.

Bessemer has been well-known as a leading VC in the SaaS era , with a particular knack for picking enterprise winners, like Box, Docusign, and Gainsight. Since 2022, it has invested in more than 260 AI-native companies. So far, the firm has invested $3 billion into AI-related startups, it says, including those focused on compute, infrastructure, foundation models, dev tools, app-layer startups, and agentic tech.

Now, Bessemer positions all things AI as the opportunity of a lifetime — a common sentiment, until the next big trendy tech revolution comes around, of course.

“AI-native companies are scaling faster than any category of technology we’ve backed before,” Bessemer Partner Byron Deeter said in the company’s funding announcement. VC firms also need to keep increasing their war chests, Deeter told Bloomberg , because companies staying private longer has become “a permanent structural shift.”

발표는 구글과 합동 세션으로 진행했다. 삼성전자는 예년 스냅드래곤 서밋처럼 핵심 디바이스 제조 파트너로 소개됐다. 스마트폰을 넘어 스마트워치, 안경, 헤드셋 등 다양한 기기로 진화하는 온디바이스 에이전틱(Agentic) AI 시장을 선점하기 위한 행보 다.

3사는 반도체, 소프트웨어, 완제품으로 역할을 분담한다. 퀄컴이 연산 능력과 AI 처리 기능을 지원하는 전용 칩셋을 공급하면, 구글은 자사 생성형 AI 제미나이(Gemini)에 맞춘 플랫폼 '안드로이드 XR(Android XR)'을 제공한다. 삼성전자는 이를 탑재한 하드웨어 폼팩터를 설계·양산하며 완제품 생태계를 완성하는 형태다.

이날 샤람 이자디 구글 XR 부문 부사장은 "제미나이 시대를 맞아 삼성, 퀄컴과 함께 안드로이드 XR 플랫폼을 구축했다"며 3각 공조를 강조했다. 그는 "스냅드래곤 XR2 2세대를 탑재한 삼성 갤럭시 XR을 통해 무한한 가상 작업 공간과 고화질 엔터테인먼트, 3D 페인팅 등 몰입형 환경을 제미나이와 함께 활용하게 될 것"이라고 설명했다.

기기 다변화 성과도 공개됐다. 아스가르 부사장은 "에이전틱 AI 시대에는 무조건적 성능 향상보다 '효율적인 지능'이 필수"라며, 스냅드래곤 AR1과 AR1 플러스 플랫폼이 세계 최초로 '멀티모달 1비트(1-bit) 모델'을 지원한다고 발표했다. 프리스미얼(Prism-EMIL)과 협력해 메모리 사용량을 크게 줄여, 가벼운 안경 폼팩터에서도 실시간 번역이나 시각 기반 어시스턴트 등 무거운 AI 모델을 기기 자체에서 구동할 수 있다.

구글도 초저전력 칩셋을 활용한 스마트 안경 대중화 청사진을 밝혔다. 이자디 부사장은 젠틀몬스터, 와비파커 등 패션 아이웨어 브랜드와 협력해 스냅드래곤 AR1 기반 지능형 안경을 올해 말 출시할 예정이라고 덧붙였다.

3사는 단일 기기 중심 사용성을 넘어 일상 전반으로 기기 간 연계를 확장할 방침이다. 아스가르 부사장은 "퍼스널 AI를 생태계 전반으로 확장하는 과정에서 삼성은 중요 파트너"라며 "스마트폰을 주머니에 넣은 채로 사용자 시야와 음성을 실시간 공유하며 맥락을 파악하는 웨어러블 기기가 진정한 개인화 AI 기반"이라고 밝혔다.

items.title: Microsoft refreshes its smaller Surface Pro and Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus
items.summary: Microsoft is refreshing its Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch devices with Qualcomm's latest Snapdragon X2 Plus chips. The smaller Surface devices retain the same design and hardware features from last year, with faster and more capable chips inside and higher price
items.content:
The Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch both have better battery life and performance, but higher price tags.

Microsoft is refreshing its Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch devices with Qualcomm’s latest Snapdragon X2 Plus chips. The smaller Surface devices retain the same design and hardware features from last year, with faster and more capable chips inside and higher price tags (thanks RAMageddon !).

While the 12-inch Surface Pro started at $799.99 last year , it’s debuting on October 13th at a starting price of $1,149.99. Likewise, the 13-inch Surface Laptop was originally priced at $899.99 , but it’s up to $1,199.99 this time around. There’s no base 8GB model this time, causing some of the price increase, as both devices launch with a minimum of 16GB of RAM and can be configured up to 24GB.

Pricing aside, Microsoft is promising that the six-core Snapdragon X2 Plus chips will deliver up to 18 percent more efficient battery performance, more than 60 percent faster graphics performance, and up to 95 percent faster local AI inferencing on the built-in NPU.

That’s a lot of percentages, but what it equates to on these devices is better battery life and improved performance. On the Surface Pro 12-inch Second Edition, as Microsoft calls it, that means an extra hour of web browsing (up to 13 hours in total), and on the Surface Laptop 13-inch Second Edition it’s two extra hours of web browsing usage (up to 18 hours in total).

Microsoft is using similar displays on these models as last year, so the Surface Pro 12-inch has a 2196 x 1464 (220 PPI) LCD display that runs at up to 90Hz. The Surface Laptop 13-inch still ships with a 1920 x 1280 (178 PPI) display that only runs at 60Hz. Both displays have been upgraded from 400 nits of brightness to 500 nits, though.

Port selection remains the same, too. Both devices include two USB-C 3.2 ports, and the Surface Laptop 13-inch also has a USB-A 3.2 port and a 3.5mm headphone jack. Both also support Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4 connectivity.

I’m surprised that Microsoft hasn’t upgraded at least one of these smaller Surface devices with a haptic trackpad, particularly because Windows 11 now adds subtle haptic nudges , and the Surface Laptop Ultra ships with haptic feedback. Microsoft is launching a second edition of its Surface Mouse with integrated haptics, and you can read all about that here .

Microsoft is also bringing back the black color option for both of these smaller Surface devices, with platinum silver or violet colors available too. Both devices will also be sold to commercial customers, and the Surface Pro 12-inch will be available in an optional 5G configuration.

items.title: Microsoft’s new Surface Mouse has haptic feedback and a customizable action button
items.summary: Microsoft is launching a second generation of its Surface Mouse next month that includes haptic feedback support. The Surface Mouse also has a customizable action button for the first time, which is primarily designed for quick access to Copilot (of course), but can be configured
items.content:
The $79.99 Surface Mouse will start shipping on October 13th.

Microsoft is launching a second generation of its Surface Mouse next month that includes haptic feedback support. The Surface Mouse also has a customizable action button for the first time, which is primarily designed for quick access to Copilot ( of course ), but can be configured to work with other shortcuts from the Surface app.

“Its haptic feedback adds a small, purposeful physical response to the moment you usually only see on a screen: a click registering, a window snapping into place or an object aligning just right,” says Brett Ostrum , corporate vice president of Surface Devices. “It is subtle by design, but noticeable within seconds — and hard to give up once you have it.”

The haptic feedback works with things like clicks, drags, and alignment throughout Windows 11, but the tactile feedback also triggers in apps like PowerPoint, Affinity, Concepts, and Filmora. Microsoft added support for haptic feedback in Windows 11 earlier this year , and so far it’s mainly Microsoft and Logitech that are supporting it with dedicated hardware. Logitech’s MX Master 4 has haptic feedback, and its Pro X2 Superstrike (and today’s new X3 ) includes a haptic-based clicks system that doesn’t support the Windows 11 haptic feedback. The upcoming Surface Laptop Ultra also has a haptic trackpad.

After originally launching the Surface Mouse in 2016 and not updating it since, Microsoft has now redesigned it to be more comfortable for all-day use, with a soft-touch material at the top. Thanks to Bluetooth 6.0 support, you can now also pair it with up to three devices.

The new Surface Mouse will be available on October 13th, the same day Microsoft launches its refreshed Surface Pro 12-inch and Surface Laptop 13-inch devices . It will be priced at $79.99, and available in black and platinum color options.

items.summary: [지디넷코리아][마우이(미국)=지디넷코리아 전화평 기자] 퀄컴이 파운데이션 모델 전문 기업 '리퀴드 AI(Liquid AI)'와 손잡고 스마트폰 기기 단에서 사용자의 일상을 파악해 스스로 행동하는 '선제적(Proactive) 에이전트' 생태계 구축에 전격 나선다.크리스티아노 아몬 퀄컴 최고경영자(CEO)는 24일(현지시간) 미국 하와이 마우이에서 열린 '스냅드래곤 서밋 2026' 기조연설에서 라민 하사니 리퀴드 AI CEO와 대담을 갖고 기기 단에서 선제적으로 작동하는 AI 에이전트의 청사진을 제
items.content:
[스냅드래곤 서밋 2026] 스냅드래곤 전용 '리퀴드 컨텍스트' 첫선…벤츠 탑재 등 로컬 AI 가속화

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/09/24 04:58 수정: 2026/09/24 08:43

[마우이(미국)=지디넷코리아 전화평 기자] 퀄컴이 파운데이션 모델 기업 '리퀴드 AI(Liquid AI)'와 손잡고 스마트폰 기기 단에서 사용자 일상을 파악해 스스로 행동하는 '선제(Proactive) 에이전트' 생태계 구축에 나선다.

크리스티아노 아몬 퀄컴 최고경영자(CEO)는 24일(현지시간) 미국 하와이 마우이에서 열린 '스냅드래곤 서밋 2026' 기조연설에서 라민 하사니 리퀴드 AI CEO와 대담을 갖고 기기 단에서 선제 작동하는 AI 에이전트 청사진을 제시했다. 이날 리퀴드 AI는 기기 간 AI 시스템 이동을 돕는 스마트 메모리 계층 '리퀴드 컨텍스트(Liquid Context)'를 스냅드래곤 기반으로 최초 공개했다.

리퀴드 컨텍스트는 스냅드래곤의 신경망처리장치(NPU)에서 구동된다. 사용자 허락 후 슬랙 메시지, 메모, 사진 등 모든 데이터를 센싱해 개인 맥락을 파악하는 것이 특징이다.

하사니 CEO는 "단순히 요청에 반응하는 것을 넘어, 평소 습관을 파악해 알아서 소셜 미디어 게시물 초안을 작성해 두는 등 일상에 적극 개입한다"고 설명했다. 현재 메르세데스-벤츠와 파트너십으로 차량 내 지능 구현에도 스냅드래곤 칩 기반 에이전트가 적용되고 있다.

리퀴드 AI가 온디바이스 생태계의 핵심 파트너로 스냅드래곤을 선택한 이유는 '이기종(Heterogeneous) 아키텍처' 조화에 있다. 하사니 CEO는 "사용자와 함께하며 상시 정보를 수집하려면 강력한 온디바이스 시스템이 필수"라며 "에이전트 구동은 헥사곤 NPU, 데이터 센싱은 센싱 허브, 샘플링은 CPU로 분담해 효율을 극대화할 수 있었다"고 강조했다. 리퀴드 AI가 개발한 2세대 파운데이션 모델 역시 이미 퀄컴 칩에 완벽히 최적화했다.

두 CEO는 AI 미래가 훈련이 끝난 '고정형 모델'에서, 끊임없이 진화하는 '평생 학습자(Lifelong learners)'로 이동할 것이라고 입을 모았다. 기존 AI가 학습이 끝난 시점의 스냅샷(고정형)에 불과했다면, 미래 에이전틱 AI는 프로덕션(상용화) 단계에서도 사용자의 변하는 취향에 맞춰 끝없이 적응해야 한다는 의미다.

하사니 CEO는 "모델의 '규모(Scale)'가 역량을 부여한다면, 모델의 '적응성(Adaptability)'은 진정한 의미의 개인화를 가능하게 한다"고 설명했다.

아몬 CEO는 기기(에지)에서 일어나는 이러한 적응과 개인화 덕분에 클라우드와 로컬 기기가 완벽한 하이브리드 형태로 작동할 것이라고 내다봤다. 아몬 CEO는 "결국 모든 사람이 자신만의 고유한 기기와 맥락을 갖게 되므로, 클라우드와 에지의 대결 구도를 논하는 것은 더 이상 무의미하다"며 "기기와 사용자가 존재하는 그 접점에서 진정한 AI 적응과 혁신이 일어날 것"이라고 강조했다.

items.title: YouTube promises custom feeds and a lot more AI later this year
items.summary: YouTube's next year could change the content you see with a big focus on AI and livestreams.
items.content:
The annual Made on YouTube event has just wrapped up, offering an early look at the features you can expect to come to Google’s dominant online streaming platform in the coming months. Yes, there’s plenty of AI for both viewers and creators, but there’s also a handful of non-AI updates mixed in there, too.

The design of YouTube’s homepage feed comes under fire often, but the platform is preparing to give you more options. With Custom Feeds, you’ll be able to add new tabs to the YouTube interface with content of your choice. To create a feed, just type a description and let YouTube populate the page. You can refine your description and rate video suggestions to tune the Custom Feed. Google says you’ll be able to save “multiple” feeds without specifying the exact number. This feature will roll out soon in the US for web, mobile, and TV users.

Interacting on YouTube will also change later this year. The platform will finally add the option to post GIFs in comments, which has apparently been a common request for some time. The comment box will let you search for popular animated thumbnails and post them on both regular videos and YouTube Shorts. The YouTube direct messaging feature is also adding support for group chat, but it’s only going to be available in the US, UK, Singapore, Brazil, and some European countries to start.

Credit: Google Credit: Google

YouTube is probably going to nudge you to chat with a robot more often, too. The AI-powered Ask YouTube feature is not new, but it’s getting several new features that will make it more prominent across the platform. The AI will take on a conversational role in product review videos, allowing you to type or use voice commands to get more information about a product. In search, Ask YouTube may offer organized video recommendations and product comparison tables, too.

The music version of this AI is also expanding. Ask Music is getting more prominent placement in the YouTube Music app, right at the top where search used to be (it recently moved to a tab at the bottom). Ask Music can create or edit playlists and tell you about an artist. It will also surface suggestions throughout the app, like when you’re creating a mix.

According to Google, YouTube creators are very invested in AI tools. The company claims that a large majority of US video posters have used AI to create or edit content in the past year. YouTube will give them even more opportunities to use AI with a new Gemini-based conversational editing feature in the YouTube Create app. After cutting together different versions of a video with AI, expanded A/B testing will let creators run up to three different versions to find the one that gets the most engagement.

A new tool called Ask Studio can also help with recommendations for things like pacing, framing, and thumbnails. It will even generate those thumbnails using AI. This tool can run in the background to analyze older videos and suggest ways to boost them for more views.

The content you see on YouTube may also change thanks to some new creator features. YouTube previously rolled out the option for two different creators to share a single livestream. Early next year, YouTube will use live matchmaking to merge streams from people who might not even know each other.

These shared streams will connect to a new feature called Live Showdown, which is billed as an interactive audience experience. Streamers will compete with a live leaderboard to see who can get the most chats, gifts, and Super Chats. So whoever gets viewers to spend the most money “wins,” essentially. Someone in this equation is probably losing, but it’s not the streamers.

The last creator update could make more content accessible to you on YouTube. The company says 40 percent of live watch time comes from viewers outside the creator’s home country. YouTube will support this trend with live autodubbing. Starting early next year, video makers will be able to enable real-time translation of their streams so viewers in other countries will be able to watch live in their preferred language. YouTube didn’t specify how this will work behind the scenes, but Google did recently release an improved Gemini translation model . So autodubbing will probably use some version of that.

items.title: Enveda secures $311M to bring more nature-derived AI drugs into clinical trials
items.summary: The round valued the AI biotech at $2 billion. It is currently testing drugs that treat skin conditions and preserve weight loss after stopping GLP-1s.
items.content:
Enveda , a biotech startup that uses AI to discover new drugs in the natural world, has raised a $311 million Series E at a $2 billion valuation. The fresh funding, which was led by Catalio Capital Management, with participation from Iconiq and others, doubles the valuation Enveda achieved 12 months ago.

The idea behind Enveda is that powerful medicines could be harnessed from plants and microbes, rather than synthesized from scratch in a lab. Viswa Colluru, an early employee of Recursion Pharmaceuticals, founded Enveda in 2019 to speed up the process of discovering these new drugs using AI and other techniques.

While AI hasn’t yet produced any FDA-approved drugs, Enveda is among the wave of companies advancing AI-discovered candidates into human clinical trials. The startup is currently testing several drugs in patients, including one targeting severe skin conditions and another designed to help maintain weight loss after stopping GLP-1s.

items.title: Modal Motors is trying to cut China out of electric motors entirely
items.summary: The startup is working on small, light motors with no rare-earth magnets that are suited for drones, fans, and robots.
items.content:
Lately, it seems like everyone is talking about bringing manufacturing back to the United States, especially when it comes to hard tech like drones and robotics. Michael Van Steenburg thinks he’s ahead of the game.

Van Steenburg spent the last decade building all kinds of electric motors in the U.S. and North America, and now he wants to do it again with his new startup, Modal Motors . This time, he wants to ditch rare-earth magnets entirely, in a bid to further separate the U.S. from China’s supply chain.

As one of the founders in Startup Battlefield 200 who will compete at TechCrunch Disrupt next month, he thinks it’s an urgent pitch to make.

“China’s already flexed its muscles a couple times,” Van Steenburg said, referring to the country restricting access to rare-earth products .

There are other companies working on setting up electric motor manufacturing and supply chains in the U.S., but Van Steenburg argues they’re doing it the wrong way by continuing to rely on rare-earth magnets. Domestic supply of those materials is still years away, he said.

“Other people are ‘reshoring,’ [but] they’re basically knocking off Chinese motors and just doing it in the U.S. But they’re hoping that the U.S. rare-earth magnet system is going to get up to speed fast enough,” he said. “It’s going to still be a while longer before they can actually replace China.”

Modal Motors has two products that it’s developing ahead of Disrupt. One is a small electric motor meant for drones that can also work in fans, blowers, and even actuators. It’s designed to “minimize mass while delivering maximum torque density and efficiency,” according to the startup’s website.

The more radical design is what Modal refers to as the “Hybrid Enigma Drive,” a planar — or flat — electric motor that can fit in lower-profile spaces.

Van Steenburg is drawing on decades of experience in the automotive industry to develop these motors and get them customer-ready. But there’s also an irony in the work Van Steenburg is doing to make Modal Motors’ products a China-free option; in the late 1990s, he worked on a hybrid gas-electric drivetrain that China wanted to put in its so-called “People’s Car.”

“It’s kind of comical,” he said, thinking back on that experience and how much the world has changed. What hasn’t changed, he said, is his outsider streak and strong conviction about doing things that are hard.

“I always tell people that the clock started ticking 25 years ago, and in that whole time, I’ve watched a slow-motion train wreck as China’s been going around the world, grabbing mines, grabbing mineral rights, doing all these things, and slowly but surely monopolizing the entire rare-earth supply chain,” he said.
